Title: VM Lifecycle
Description: Understand the states a VM passes through from creation to deletion, including suspend, stop, and snapshot.
Content:
---
title: VM Lifecycle
description: Understand the states a VM passes through from creation to deletion, including suspend, stop, and snapshot.
---
import { Mermaid } from "../../../../src/components/mermaid";

<Callout type="warn">
  VMs default to **sticky** persistence, which means they will be automatically cleaned up when they aren't running. If you need a VM to persist indefinitely, set `persistence: { type: "persistent" }` when creating it. See [Persistence](/v2/vms/lifecycle/persistence) for details on all persistence types and what they mean.
</Callout>

### State Transitions

VMs move between three active states. Suspended VMs resume instantly with full memory intact. Stopped VMs lose memory and boot fresh — only use `stop()` when you need a reboot.

<Mermaid chart={`%%{init: {"flowchart": {"nodeSpacing": 80, "rankSpacing": 80}} }%%
flowchart LR
    Init((Start)) -->|"create()"| Running
    Running -->|"suspend() / idle timeout"| Suspended
    Running -->|"stop()"| Stopped
    Suspended -->|"start() / network / SSH"| Running
    Stopped -->|"start()"| Running
`} />

### Snapshots

Any active state can be snapshotted or deleted. With `recreate` enabled, deleted VMs and snapshots are automatically rebuilt when needed.

<Mermaid chart={`%%{init: {"flowchart": {"nodeSpacing": 80, "rankSpacing": 80}} }%%
flowchart TB
    Running -->|"snapshot()"| Snapshot
    Suspended -->|"snapshot()"| Snapshot
    Stopped -->|"snapshot()"| Snapshot
    Snapshot -->|"create() from snapshot"| Running
    Snapshot -->|"delete()"| DeletedSnapshot[Deleted Snapshot]
    DeletedSnapshot -.->|"recreate"| Snapshot
    Running -->|"delete()"| Deleted
    Suspended -->|"delete()"| Deleted
    Stopped -->|"delete()"| Deleted
    Deleted -.->|"start() with recreate"| Running
`} />

## States

### Running

The VM is actively executing, consuming CPU and memory. This is the state a VM enters immediately after `create()`.

```ts
import { freestyle } from "freestyle-sandboxes";

const { vm } = await freestyle.vms.create();
// VM is now running
await vm.exec("echo 'hello'");
```

### Suspended

The VM's full memory and CPU state is saved to disk, then the VM is paused. When resumed, it continues from the exact point it left off — no reboot, no lost state.

Suspension happens either explicitly or automatically via idle timeout:

```ts
// Explicit suspend
await vm.suspend();

// Auto-suspend after 5 minutes of network inactivity
const { vm } = await freestyle.vms.create({
  idleTimeoutSeconds: 300,
});
```

While suspended you are **not billed for CPU or memory** — only storage.

A suspended VM resumes automatically on:
- Calling `vm.start()`
- Incoming network activity (e.g. an HTTP request to a mapped port)
- An SSH connection
- Running a command with `vm.exec()`

```ts
// Explicitly resume
await vm.start();
```

### Stopped

The VM is shut down gracefully (like powering off a machine). The disk is preserved but memory state is lost. On next `start()`, the VM boots fresh from its disk. Most of the time you should use `suspend()` instead — `stop()` is only needed when you explicitly want a full reboot.

```ts
await vm.stop();

// Later — boots from disk
await vm.start();
```

### Killed

For cases where you need to force-terminate a VM immediately without a graceful shutdown:

```ts
await vm.kill();
```

## Suspend vs Stop

| | Suspend | Stop |
|---|---|---|
| **Memory state** | Preserved — resumes exactly where it left off | Lost — boots fresh from disk |
| **Resume speed** | Under 100ms | Full boot (3–7 seconds) |
| **Billing** | Storage only | Storage only |
| **Use case** | Almost everything — the default way to pause a VM | Only when you explicitly want a full reboot |
| **Auto trigger** | Idle timeout | — |

**Suspend is almost always what you want.** It's faster, preserves state, and costs the same as stop. The only reason to use `stop()` is when you explicitly need to reboot the VM — for example to reset a corrupted process tree.

## Snapshots

A snapshot captures the entire VM state (memory, disk, CPU registers) as an immutable image. Snapshots can be taken from any state — running, suspended, or stopped.

```ts
const { snapshotId } = await vm.snapshot();

// Create new VMs from the snapshot
const { vm: clone1 } = await freestyle.vms.create({ snapshotId });
const { vm: clone2 } = await freestyle.vms.create({ snapshotId });
```

Snapshots are replicated across the network for fast creation anywhere. See [Specs and Snapshots](/v2/vms/templates-snapshots) for declarative snapshot creation and layering.

## Forking

A running VM can be forked without noticeably pausing the original. This creates a new VM that is an exact copy of the current state.

```ts
const { vm: forked } = await vm.fork();
```

Use forking when you need one-off copies for parallel exploration. Use snapshots when you need a reusable base image.

## Idle Timeout

Automatically suspend VMs after a period of network inactivity (default: 300 seconds):

```ts
const { vm } = await freestyle.vms.create({
  idleTimeoutSeconds: 600, // 10 minutes
});
```

Set to `null` to disable idle timeout:

```ts
const { vm } = await freestyle.vms.create({
  idleTimeoutSeconds: null, // Never auto-suspend
});
```

> **Cost consideration:** VMs with no idle timeout continue running (and billing) indefinitely. Use [persistence](/v2/vms/lifecycle/persistence) settings to control storage costs when suspended.

## Deletion

Delete a VM to permanently remove it and free all resources:

```ts
await freestyle.vms.delete({ vmId });
```

## Waiting for Exit

If a VM is running a finite workload, you can block until it exits:

```ts
const result = await vm.waitForExit();
```

## Common Patterns

### Development VM with long timeout
```ts
const { vm } = await freestyle.vms.create({
  workdir: "/workspace",
  idleTimeoutSeconds: 3600, // 1 hour
  gitRepos: [
    { repo: repoId, path: "/workspace" },
  ],
});
```

### Production VM (never suspend)
```ts
const { vm } = await freestyle.vms.create({
  idleTimeoutSeconds: null,
  persistence: { type: "persistent" },
  waitForReadySignal: true,
});
```

### Serverless-style VM
```ts
const { vm } = await freestyle.vms.create({
  recreate: true,
  idleTimeoutSeconds: 60, // Suspend quickly
  persistence: { type: "ephemeral" },
});
```

---
title: VM Lifecycle
description: Understand the states a VM passes through from creation to deletion, including suspend, stop, and snapshot.
---
import { Mermaid } from "../../../../src/components/mermaid";

<Callout type="warn">
  VMs default to **sticky** persistence, which means they will be automatically cleaned up when they aren't running. If you need a VM to persist indefinitely, set `persistence: { type: "persistent" }` when creating it. See [Persistence](/v2/vms/lifecycle/persistence) for details on all persistence types and what they mean.
</Callout>

### State Transitions

VMs move between three active states. Suspended VMs resume instantly with full memory intact. Stopped VMs lose memory and boot fresh — only use `stop()` when you need a reboot.

<Mermaid chart={`%%{init: {"flowchart": {"nodeSpacing": 80, "rankSpacing": 80}} }%%
flowchart LR
    Init((Start)) -->|"create()"| Running
    Running -->|"suspend() / idle timeout"| Suspended
    Running -->|"stop()"| Stopped
    Suspended -->|"start() / network / SSH"| Running
    Stopped -->|"start()"| Running
`} />

### Snapshots

Any active state can be snapshotted or deleted. With `recreate` enabled, deleted VMs and snapshots are automatically rebuilt when needed.

<Mermaid chart={`%%{init: {"flowchart": {"nodeSpacing": 80, "rankSpacing": 80}} }%%
flowchart TB
    Running -->|"snapshot()"| Snapshot
    Suspended -->|"snapshot()"| Snapshot
    Stopped -->|"snapshot()"| Snapshot
    Snapshot -->|"create() from snapshot"| Running
    Snapshot -->|"delete()"| DeletedSnapshot[Deleted Snapshot]
    DeletedSnapshot -.->|"recreate"| Snapshot
    Running -->|"delete()"| Deleted
    Suspended -->|"delete()"| Deleted
    Stopped -->|"delete()"| Deleted
    Deleted -.->|"start() with recreate"| Running
`} />

## States

### Running

The VM is actively executing, consuming CPU and memory. This is the state a VM enters immediately after `create()`.

```ts
import { freestyle } from "freestyle-sandboxes";

const { vm } = await freestyle.vms.create();
// VM is now running
await vm.exec("echo 'hello'");
```

### Suspended

The VM's full memory and CPU state is saved to disk, then the VM is paused. When resumed, it continues from the exact point it left off — no reboot, no lost state.

Suspension happens either explicitly or automatically via idle timeout:

```ts
// Explicit suspend
await vm.suspend();

// Auto-suspend after 5 minutes of network inactivity
const { vm } = await freestyle.vms.create({
  idleTimeoutSeconds: 300,
});
```

While suspended you are **not billed for CPU or memory** — only storage.

A suspended VM resumes automatically on:
- Calling `vm.start()`
- Incoming network activity (e.g. an HTTP request to a mapped port)
- An SSH connection
- Running a command with `vm.exec()`

```ts
// Explicitly resume
await vm.start();
```

### Stopped

The VM is shut down gracefully (like powering off a machine). The disk is preserved but memory state is lost. On next `start()`, the VM boots fresh from its disk. Most of the time you should use `suspend()` instead — `stop()` is only needed when you explicitly want a full reboot.

```ts
await vm.stop();

// Later — boots from disk
await vm.start();
```

### Killed

For cases where you need to force-terminate a VM immediately without a graceful shutdown:

```ts
await vm.kill();
```

## Suspend vs Stop

| | Suspend | Stop |
|---|---|---|
| **Memory state** | Preserved — resumes exactly where it left off | Lost — boots fresh from disk |
| **Resume speed** | Under 100ms | Full boot (3–7 seconds) |
| **Billing** | Storage only | Storage only |
| **Use case** | Almost everything — the default way to pause a VM | Only when you explicitly want a full reboot |
| **Auto trigger** | Idle timeout | — |

**Suspend is almost always what you want.** It's faster, preserves state, and costs the same as stop. The only reason to use `stop()` is when you explicitly need to reboot the VM — for example to reset a corrupted process tree.

## Snapshots

A snapshot captures the entire VM state (memory, disk, CPU registers) as an immutable image. Snapshots can be taken from any state — running, suspended, or stopped.

```ts
const { snapshotId } = await vm.snapshot();

// Create new VMs from the snapshot
const { vm: clone1 } = await freestyle.vms.create({ snapshotId });
const { vm: clone2 } = await freestyle.vms.create({ snapshotId });
```

Snapshots are replicated across the network for fast creation anywhere. See [Specs and Snapshots](/v2/vms/templates-snapshots) for declarative snapshot creation and layering.

## Forking

A running VM can be forked without noticeably pausing the original. This creates a new VM that is an exact copy of the current state.

```ts
const { vm: forked } = await vm.fork();
```

Use forking when you need one-off copies for parallel exploration. Use snapshots when you need a reusable base image.

## Idle Timeout

Automatically suspend VMs after a period of network inactivity (default: 300 seconds):

```ts
const { vm } = await freestyle.vms.create({
  idleTimeoutSeconds: 600, // 10 minutes
});
```

Set to `null` to disable idle timeout:

```ts
const { vm } = await freestyle.vms.create({
  idleTimeoutSeconds: null, // Never auto-suspend
});
```

> **Cost consideration:** VMs with no idle timeout continue running (and billing) indefinitely. Use [persistence](/v2/vms/lifecycle/persistence) settings to control storage costs when suspended.

## Deletion

Delete a VM to permanently remove it and free all resources:

```ts
await freestyle.vms.delete({ vmId });
```

## Waiting for Exit

If a VM is running a finite workload, you can block until it exits:

```ts
const result = await vm.waitForExit();
```

## Common Patterns

### Development VM with long timeout
```ts
const { vm } = await freestyle.vms.create({
  workdir: "/workspace",
  idleTimeoutSeconds: 3600, // 1 hour
  gitRepos: [
    { repo: repoId, path: "/workspace" },
  ],
});
```

### Production VM (never suspend)
```ts
const { vm } = await freestyle.vms.create({
  idleTimeoutSeconds: null,
  persistence: { type: "persistent" },
  waitForReadySignal: true,
});
```

### Serverless-style VM
```ts
const { vm } = await freestyle.vms.create({
  recreate: true,
  idleTimeoutSeconds: 60, // Suspend quickly
  persistence: { type: "ephemeral" },
});
```

Use the Freestyle CLI for operational VM workflows and quick debugging.

## Prerequisites

- Set `FREESTYLE_API_KEY` in your environment.
- Run commands as `npx freestyle-sandboxes ...`.

## Core workflows

### List VMs

```bash
npx freestyle-sandboxes vm list
```

### Create from snapshot and run one command

```bash
npx freestyle-sandboxes vm create \
  --snapshot <snapshot-id> \
  --exec '<command>'
```

### Create, run one command, and auto-cleanup

```bash
npx freestyle-sandboxes vm create \
  --snapshot <snapshot-id> \
  --exec '<command>' \
  --delete
```

### Open an interactive SSH session

```bash
npx freestyle-sandboxes vm create --snapshot <snapshot-id> --ssh
```

For temporary debug sessions:

```bash
npx freestyle-sandboxes vm create --snapshot <snapshot-id> --ssh --delete
```

### Exec on an existing VM

```bash
npx freestyle-sandboxes vm exec <vm-id> '<command>'
```

### Delete a VM

```bash
npx freestyle-sandboxes vm delete <vm-id>
```

## Common options

- `--json`: return machine-readable output.
- `--delete`:
  - with `--ssh`: delete when SSH session exits.
  - without `--ssh`: delete after create/exec completes.

## Debugging systemd startup failures

For `VM_SETUP_FAILED`, capture logs immediately from a fresh VM:

```bash
npx freestyle-sandboxes vm create \
  --snapshot <snapshot-id> \
  --exec 'journalctl --no-pager -eu <service-name>' \
  --delete
```

See [Systemd Services](/v2/vms/configuration/systemd-services#debugging-failed-services) for the full troubleshooting flow.

```bash
npx freestyle-sandboxes vm create --snapshot <snapshot-id> --ssh
```

For temporary debug sessions:

```bash
npx freestyle-sandboxes vm create --snapshot <snapshot-id> --ssh --delete
```

### Exec on an existing VM

```bash
npx freestyle-sandboxes vm exec <vm-id> '<command>'
```

### Delete a VM

```bash
npx freestyle-sandboxes vm delete <vm-id>
```

## Common options

- `--json`: return machine-readable output.
- `--delete`:
  - with `--ssh`: delete when SSH session exits.
  - without `--ssh`: delete after create/exec completes.

## Debugging systemd startup failures

For `VM_SETUP_FAILED`, capture logs immediately from a fresh VM:

```bash
npx freestyle-sandboxes vm create \
  --snapshot <snapshot-id> \
  --exec 'journalctl --no-pager -eu <service-name>' \
  --delete
```

See [Systemd Services](/v2/vms/configuration/systemd-services#debugging-failed-services) for the full troubleshooting flow.
